question: In a high-anion gap metabolic acidosis, a delta-delta ratio (Δ anion gap / Δ HCO₃⁻) greater than 2 suggests an underlying metabolic alkalosis coexisting with the high-anion gap acidosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Delta-delta ratio = (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃⁻). A ratio >2 means the AG rise outpaces the bicarbonate fall, indicating a concurrent metabolic alkalosis. A ratio <1 suggests an additional normal-AG acidosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The delta-delta ratio compares how much the AG has risen above normal with how much HCO₃⁻ has fallen. If the AG has risen more than expected (ratio >2), the HCO₃⁻ has not fallen as much as expected — meaning a concurrent metabolic alkalosis is partially protecting the bicarbonate.
